publisher: U.S. House Committee on Homeland Security
title: Chairmen Garbarino, Moolenaar Announce Joint Investigation into National Security Risks Posed by PRC AI Models
date_evidence:
Chairmen Garbarino, Moolenaar Announce Joint Investigation into National Security Risks Posed by PRC AI Models

April 29, 2026

WASHINGTON, D.C.
key_claim: Joint House investigation: in late 2024 PRC-developed models reportedly accounted for an estimated one percent of global AI workloads; by end-2025 that share had reportedly grown to an estimated 30 percent. Names DeepSeek, Alibaba, Moonshot AI, MiniMax; cites Airbnb relying on Qwen ('fast and cheap') and Cursor's Composer 2 reportedly built on a Moonshot open-weight model; frames passive reliance on PRC-origin AI as a national-security choice, not a neutral commercial decision.
verbatim_quote: In late 2024, PRC models reportedly accounted for an estimated one percent of global AI workloads. By the end of 2025, that share had reportedly grown to an estimated 30 percent.
notes: Tier 1 congressional primary. Anchors the deployment-share quantification (1% -> 30% global workloads) and the national-security framing. Also references the 23 April 2026 White House OSTP (Kratsios) memo on industrial-scale distillation.

publisher: NIST / Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI)
title: CAISI Evaluation of DeepSeek V4 Pro
date_evidence:
CAISI Evaluation of DeepSeek V4 Pro

May 1, 2026 ... Released May 1, 2026, Updated May 2, 2026
key_claim: US government testing finds DeepSeek V4 Pro is the most capable PRC model CAISI has evaluated to date but its capability lags the US frontier by about 8 months; it is more cost efficient than the most cost-competitive US reference model (GPT-5.4 mini) on 5 of 7 benchmarks, ranging from 53% less expensive to 41% more expensive.
verbatim_quote: CAISI evaluations indicate that DeepSeek V4's capabilities lag behind the frontier by about 8 months
notes: Tier 1 US government primary research. Anchors both the capability-lag counter-evidence and the cost-efficiency engine of the signal.

title: The 2026 AI Index Report, Chapter 2: Technical Performance
date_evidence: Stanford HAI AI Index 2026 Summary: Adoption, Public Trust, and the U.S.-China AI Gap | by Adnan Masood, PhD. | Apr, 2026 | Medium
key_claim: As of March 2026 the top US model leads the top Chinese model by 2.7%, down from double-digit gaps in 2023; the top four firms cluster within 25 Elo points on the Arena leaderboard, shifting competition toward cost and reliability; the open-vs-closed gap reopened in 2025, with the top closed model leading the top open model by 3.3% and six of the top ten models now closed.
verbatim_quote: As of March 2026, the top U.S. model leads by 2.7%
notes: Tier 2 academic index. Report released mid-April 2026. Provides the frontier-convergence framing and the counter-evidence that US/closed models still narrowly lead the frontier.

title: Open Models, Soft Power, and the Spectrum of U.S.-China Artificial Intelligence Competition
date_evidence: Expert InsightsPublished Mar 26, 2026 ... RAND Corporation, PE-A4686-1, March 2026. As of March 26, 2026
key_claim: Open models are emerging as a critical instrument of soft power in the US-China AI competition; the authors argue the US needs stronger support for an open-model ecosystem, a recalibration of export controls, and incentives for permissive licensing to counter the influence China seeks through diffusing its technology and tech infrastructure.
notes: Tier 2 think-tank. Anchors the soft-power / diffusion-as-strategy framing and the US policy-response options.

title: Beyond DeepSeek: China's Diverse Open-Weight AI Ecosystem and Its Policy Implications
key_claim: China's open-weight LLM ecosystem is driven by a wide range of actors prioritising computationally efficient models optimised for flexible downstream deployment; Chinese-made open-weight models are now 'unavoidable' in the global competitive AI landscape and are increasingly adopted worldwide, including in the United States, with material implications for global technology dependence and AI governance.
verbatim_quote: Chinese-made open-weight models are unavoidable in the global competitive AI landscape.
notes: Structural anchor (3-6 month band). Canonical primary framing of the diverse Chinese open-weight ecosystem and deployment-optimised design.

title: Exclusive: US State Dept orders global warning about alleged AI thefts by DeepSeek, other Chinese firms
key_claim: A US State Department diplomatic cable instructs every embassy to warn host governments about extraction and distillation of US AI models, naming DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and MiniMax; many Western and some Asian governments have banned DeepSeek over data concerns, yet its models 'have consistently been among the most used' on international platforms hosting open-source models; DeepSeek launched its V4 preview adapted for Huawei chips.
verbatim_quote: DeepSeek's models have consistently been among the most used on international platforms that host open-source models.
notes: Tier 3 Reuters wire (republished via KFGO, meta-author Thomson Reuters). Source for the policy escalation and the ban-vs-usage paradox.

title: OpenRouter Rankings April 2026: Top AI Models by Data
key_claim: Analysis of OpenRouter's public usage rankings: Chinese-origin models rose from approximately 1.2% of OpenRouter token volume in October 2024 to over 45% by April 2026 (Mar 2025 ~10%, Jul 2025 ~25%, Dec 2025 ~35%); four of the top five models by weekly token volume are Chinese, with Xiaomi at 22.3% provider share and Anthropic at 15.4%.
verbatim_quote: Chinese-origin models now account for over 45% of all OpenRouter traffic, up from under 2% in late 2024
notes: Tier 4 vendor/practitioner analysis of OpenRouter public telemetry. Directional corroboration of the deployment-share trajectory on one inference marketplace; not an anchor.
